recs.stt: Photographing an exoplanet 25 light years away with 25km/pixel resolution (2020)
recs.x:
This is fascinating. There is a plan to directly photograph exoplanets by sending a series of telescopes 500+ AU in the opposite direction of what we want to photograph and using the sun as a gravitational lens. We send out waves of these small telescopes to get pictures at various focal planes.

This video has a good description of the paper: [link]

recs.stt: A solar gravitational lens will be humanity's most powerful telescope (2022)
recs.x:
Christian Ready made a great video on his Youtube channel, Launch Pad Astronomy, about NASA's plans for a solar gravitational lens. It's got some great graphics and visualisations, and is accessibly narrated. I was inspired and learnt a lot of new ideas.
